<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920245_theRebbe_641" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920245_theRebbe_641__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the maamar "Lecha Dodi" and the analogy of the groom as the King and the bride as the Queen, explaining the order of influence from the Zeir Anpin to Malchus, first external then internal.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Teitzei,</t>
    <t s="2">the 13th of Elul,</t>
    <t s="3">the year 5714*.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the groom is the Holy One, blessed be He, and the bride is the Congregation of Israel, corresponding to Zeir Anpin and Malchus, and describes the two-stage process of influence: first external and encompassing, then internal.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Come, my beloved, to meet the bride; let us welcome the presence of Shabbos,"</t>
    <t s="1">and the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings in his maamar "Lecha Dodi"</t>
    <t s="2">(from the discourses of the wedding1)</t>
    <t s="3">(from Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer2)</t>
    <t s="4">that the groom is comparable to a king and the bride to a queen.</t>
    <t s="5">This groom is the Holy One, blessed be He, and the bride is the Congregation of Israel,</t>
    <t s="6">and in the Sefiros this is the matter of Zeir Anpin and Malchus,</t>
    <t s="7">for the groom is the aspect of Zeir Anpin and the bride is the aspect of Malchus.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is "Come, my beloved, to meet the bride; let us welcome the presence of Shabbos,"</t>
    <t s="9">which is the matter of drawing down Zeir Anpin to Malchus,</t>
    <t s="10">and the order of the drawing down is,</t>
    <t s="11">that first there must be an external drawing down</t>
    <t s="12">(from Zeir Anpin to Malchus)</t>
    <t s="13">which is only in the aspect of encompassing,</t>
    <t s="14">and afterwards is the internal drawing down.</t>
    <t s="15">For such is the order in every influence from an influencer to a recipient,</t>
    <t s="16">that first there must be a drawing down of the influencer from his external aspect to the external aspect of the recipient,</t>
    <t s="17">through which the recipient is elevated to be close to the level of the influencer,</t>
    <t s="18">and afterwards he can receive the internal influence from the influencer.</t>
    <t s="19">And he brings regarding this3</t>
    <t s="20">two analogies</t>
    <t s="21">[from the influence of a teacher to a student,</t>
    <t s="22">and a father playing with his young son].</t>
    <t s="23">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="24">that his intention in these analogies is not only to bring examples of the order of influence</t>
    <t s="25">(that the external influence is a preparation for the internal influence),</t>
    <t s="26">but rather</t>
    <t s="27">(also)</t>
    <t s="28">to explain the greatness of the superiority in these two influences,</t>
    <t s="29">for even the external influence is an extremely lofty level,</t>
    <t s="30">to the point that it has a superiority over the internal influence.</t>
    <t s="31">Because the external influence,</t>
    <t s="32">which is the aspect of encompassing,</t>
    <t s="33">is above the vessel of the recipient</t>
    <t s="34">(unlike the internal influence which is received in the vessel of the recipient).</t>
    <t s="35">Nevertheless, it is only a preparation for the internal influence,</t>
    <t s="36">for specifically through the internal influence one reaches a more elevated superiority</t>
    <t s="37">(which is above the aspect of the encompassing).</t>
    <t s="38">And this is "For all honor is a wedding canopy"4</t>
    <t s="39">which are two aspects of honor,</t>
    <t s="40">the honor of the groom and the honor of the bride,</t>
    <t s="41">and on a higher level5</t>
    <t s="42">the honor of Abba and the honor of Imma.</t>
    <t s="43">And through this is the union of Abba and Imma and the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukva.</t>
    <t s="44">For despite both of them</t>
    <t s="45">(the honor</t>
    <t s="46">(and the wedding canopy)</t>
    <t s="47">of Abba and Imma,</t>
    <t s="48">and the honor</t>
    <t s="49">(and the wedding canopy)</t>
    <t s="50">of Zeir Anpin and Nukva)</t>
    <t s="51">being aspects of encompassing,</t>
    <t s="52">nevertheless it is known6</t>
    <t s="53">that specifically in the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukva</t>
    <t s="54">(which is an internal union)</t>
    <t s="55">the Essence (Atzmus) is drawn down.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section elaborates on the first analogy of a teacher and student, explaining that the preliminary joke (a lighthearted word) is an external influence that opens the heart and mind, and its source is in the simple pleasure that is above the pleasure of intellect, yet the internal influence reaches the essential, unfeeling pleasure.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the first analogy is from the influence of a teacher to a student,</t>
    <t s="2">and the order of influence is as our sages, of blessed memory, said7</t>
    <t s="3">that before he would open [the lesson] for the sages, he would say a humorous thing and the sages would laugh, and finally he would sit in awe and open the discourse,</t>
    <t s="4">for the humorous thing that precedes the study</t>
    <t s="5">[which is the matter of the mundane conversation of Torah scholars which requires study8]</t>
    <t s="6">is only external,</t>
    <t s="7">however this influence is a preparation for the internal influence</t>
    <t s="8">(of "opening the discourse")</t>
    <t s="9">because specifically through this the heart and mind of the student are opened to become a vessel to receive the internal influence.</t>
    <t s="10">And the source of this analogy is from the Mitteler Rebbe in Toras Chaim9</t>
    <t s="11">[except that in Toras Chaim it is not brought as an analogy for the matter of "Lecha Dodi."</t>
    <t s="12">And in the discourse "Semuchim La'ad Ad Paros"10</t>
    <t s="13">(the maamar said by the Rebbe, the Rebbe Rashab, of blessed memory, on his birthday</t>
    <t s="14">(the 20th of MarCheshvan)</t>
    <t s="15">the last one in this world)</t>
    <t s="16">he connects, in a possible manner,</t>
    <t s="17">("And it is possible that this is the matter, etc.")</t>
    <t s="18">the matter of the humorous thing to the matter of "Lecha Dodi."</t>
    <t s="19">And in the discourse "Lecha Dodi," the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, omitted the word "it is possible" and writes this simply11],</t>
    <t s="20">and in Toras Chaim there</t>
    <t s="21">(afterwards12)</t>
    <t s="22">he explains,</t>
    <t s="23">that the root of the matter of laughter is from the simple pleasure that is not composite at all.</t>
    <t s="24">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="25">that the root of the humorous thing</t>
    <t s="26">(which is the simple pleasure)</t>
    <t s="27">is above the influence of the intellect that follows</t>
    <t s="28">(for the pleasure in intellect is a composite pleasure).</t>
    <t s="29">However, nevertheless, this is only an external aspect,</t>
    <t s="30">and through the internal influence one reaches a more elevated superiority.</t>
    <t s="31">And the matter is that in the simple pleasure itself there are two levels13,</t>
    <t s="32">the felt simple pleasure and the essential, unfeeling pleasure.</t>
    <t s="33">And specifically through the internal influence,</t>
    <t s="34">which the student receives in his innerness,</t>
    <t s="35">one reaches the essential, unfeeling pleasure.</t>
    <t s="36">And therefore our sages, of blessed memory, said14</t>
    <t s="37">"And from my students more than all of them."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
